title: Implement MVP mobile app and SDK host

observation: Use structured worklog tools as the source of truth; record observations, tasks, blockers, validation, and closure; commit tracked worklog updates with source changes.
Implementation should be test-driven where practical, prefer simple direct solutions, validate only system boundaries, and pause for human clarification when genuinely blocked.
New code should use intention-revealing names, small focused functions/classes, simple error handling, and fast independent tests.

Current branch is `research/mobile-app-stack-relay-sdk` at `ae3420c`; working tree only has the newly created untracked MVP worklog. The repository currently contains only README.md aside from git/pi metadata.

Implement an MVP monorepo with pnpm workspaces containing both an iPhone-first app and an SDK-based mobile host/server; use good test coverage; attempt iOS simulator e2e with `agent-device`; merge the research branch into main first, then restart work from latest main on a new worklog/branch; README must describe the implemented repository state.

The repository has no `main` branch or remote branch; only research branches exist. To satisfy the request, create `main` at the current research tip (`ae3420c`) so the research branch is effectively merged, then branch MVP work from that latest main.

Created `main` at the research tip because no main branch existed, then created `feature/mobile-mvp-sdk-host` from main for implementation. This satisfies the request to restart work from latest main given the repository's available refs.

Current README is a research plan, not an implemented repository guide. It must be rewritten or substantially updated by the end to describe the actual pnpm monorepo, host/server API, app, tests, and run commands.

The host should use `AgentSessionRuntime` for new/resume/fork/import/switch flows, call `session.bindExtensions()` with a mobile UI context, re-subscribe/re-bind after runtime replacement, and use `PromptOptions.preflightResult` to acknowledge accepted prompts before `session.prompt()` resolves.

The Pi package exports the needed SDK symbols from its public entrypoint: `createAgentSessionRuntime`, `createAgentSessionServices`, `createAgentSessionFromServices`, `getAgentDir`, `SessionManager`, `AgentSessionRuntime`, `AgentSession`, `ExtensionUIContext`, and session event types.
`SessionManager` supports `create(cwd)`, `open(path)`, `continueRecent(cwd)`, `list(cwd)`, and `listAll()`, which are sufficient for the MVP's new/open/list session API.

Node v25.9.0, pnpm 10.33.2, npm 11.12.1, `agent-device` at `/opt/homebrew/bin/agent-device`, and `xcrun` at `/usr/bin/xcrun` are available. iOS simulator e2e should be attempted after the app can run.

`agent-device` can ensure/boot simulators, open Expo Go/dev clients, capture snapshots/screenshots, and run `.ad` suites. For an Expo MVP, likely validation path is to start Metro and open the Expo URL in an iOS simulator if dependencies/install permit.

title: Reinstall or update Expo Go on iOS simulator and rerun e2e validation

content: Investigating whether Expo Go can be reinstalled/updated on the iPhone simulator, then rerunning the host + Metro + agent-device e2e path if possible.

source: xcrun simctl uninstall + Expo CLI start
observation: Uninstalled old Expo Go from the iPhone 16 Pro simulator, then ran `CI=1 pnpm --filter @pi-mobile/app exec expo start --ios --go --localhost --port 8081`; Expo CLI fetched and installed SDK-matched Expo Go at `Expo-Go-54.0.7.tar.app` and opened `exp://127.0.0.1:8081`.

After reinstalling Expo Go, the app launched successfully in the simulator and rendered the Pi Mobile screen instead of the SDK mismatch page. The screenshot also showed the Expo developer menu overlay, confirming runtime SDK 54.0.0.

`agent-device click` and `agent-device snapshot` still failed with `IOS_RUNNER_CONNECT_TIMEOUT` / `Runner did not accept connection (simctl spawn)`, so fully automated tap/assert interaction could not be completed in this environment even though Expo Go was updated and the app launched.

content: Expo Go reinstall succeeded and the app launched in the simulator. Full automated e2e interaction remains blocked by agent-device's iOS runner connection timeout for click/snapshot commands; screenshot validation confirms the app now renders under Expo Go SDK 54.

observation: After updating README and worklog with Expo Go reinstall findings, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test`, `pnpm build`, and `git diff --check` all passed again.
Previous MVP is complete on branch `feature/mobile-mvp-sdk-host` with all tasks terminal; current feedback should be handled as a review-phase increment on the same worklog with new tasks.

The current mobile app is a single screen with connection controls, workspace cwd input, transcript, and composer all rendered together. The workspace cwd default comes from `createInitialAppViewState` as `.` and the transcript uses a light card with generic message colors.
App view state currently tracks host URL/token/cwd/prompt/connectionState but has no screen/navigation state and does not hydrate cwd from the host's absolute `HostStatus.cwd`.
`HostController.getStatus()` exposes `process.cwd()` as `HostStatus.cwd`, which can seed the mobile app's workspace path with an absolute host path after connect.

The Pi session export mobile view uses a dark terminal-like palette, monospace typography, compact line-height, cyan session title, yellow help/status text, dim gray metadata, user message cards on `#343541`, custom/system cards on purple `#2d2838`, tool cards on green/pending/error dark backgrounds, and rounded 4px blocks with ~18px rhythm.

The Pi TUI composer reference is a full-width monospaced input area on dark `#343541`-like background with thin purple top/bottom borders, a block cursor/start of prompt, and a dim status footer showing cwd/branch/model metadata.

source: Expo Web export attempt before dependencies

Added explicit opt-in CORS support via `MobileHostServerOptions.corsOrigin` / `PI_MOBILE_HOST_CORS_ORIGIN`, so Expo Web can call the host API during local smoke tests without making CORS globally implicit.

Exported the Expo app for web, served it on `http://127.0.0.1:8082`, started the host with `PI_MOBILE_HOST_CORS_ORIGIN=http://127.0.0.1:8082`, and used `agent-browser` in an iPhone 14 viewport to click Connect and Open new session. The web smoke verified the connection screen, absolute host cwd seeding, session-screen transition, Pi-style header, and TUI-like composer.
